title: Lambert W Function Framework for Graphene Nanoribbon Quantum Sensing: Theory, Verification, and Multi-Modal Applications
summary: We establish a rigorous mathematical framework connecting graphene nanoribbon quantum sensing to the Lambert W function through the finite square well (FSW) analogy. The Lambert W function, defined as the inverse of $f(W)=We^W$, provides exact analytical solutions to transcendental equations governing quantum confinement. Operating near the branch point singularity at $z=-1/e$ yields sensitivity enhancement factors scaling as $(z-z_c)^{-1/2}$, achieving 35-fold enhancement when the operating point lies within $δ=0.001$ of the branch point.
